thread.title: SFA to phase out Early Childhood Lab
thread.title_full: SFA to phase out Early Childhood Lab

author: JOSH EDWARDS The Nacogdoches Daily Sentinel
title: SFA to phase out Early Childhood Lab
text:
Editor’s note This is the first in a series of stories about the phasing out of Stephen F. Austin State University’s Early Childhood Laboratory. We are asking readers to share their experiences with the lab. Email josh.edwards@dailysentinel.com or call 936-558-3201.
Stephen F. Austin State University is phasing out its Early Childhood Laboratory, ending the more than 50-year-old program due to financial concerns.
“Ultimately, university leadership determined that the continuing operation is no longer financially sustainable,” SFA provost Jordan Barkley said in a statement announcing the phasing out of the program.
The university will no longer accept new infant enrollments beginning with the 2027-28 academic year. Classrooms will be phased out year-by-year as the program closes.
“Children currently enrolled, those who have been offered enrollment and those who receive an offer before that time will be able to remain in the program through completion,” Barkley said in the statement to SFA faculty and staff.
The statement was made public late Tuesday on the Facebook page of the SFA Early Childhood Laboratory by program director Crystal Sanders.
“I recognize this announcement brings many emotions for families, staff, students, alumni, and community members. I want our families to know that our dedicated staff remains committed to providing high-quality care, support, and learning experiences for our children throughout this process,” Sanders said.
Barkley’s statement indicated the program is continuing to lose money.
“Over the past five years, SFA has provided approximately $750,000 in institutional support to sustain the (laboratory) beyond the revenue generated by tuition and fees,” Barkley said. “Financial projections indicate the university would need to invest approximately $1.5 million over the next 10 years to continue operating the laboratory.”
What is the lab?
The Early Childhood Laboratory opened at Stephen F. Austin State University in 1975. The program provides education to students ages 2 months to 5 years and also serves as a training ground for teachers. The lab has approximately 72 students enrolled right now.
Classrooms have two teachers — one with a master’s degree and the other with a bachelor’s, said retired Early Childhood Laboratory teacher Karen Briley Bethel.
“If you were a master teacher, you would go upstairs and teach the college lab,” she said. “Those groups would come into our classrooms and do live lessons.”
The program moved into its current location in 2009 with the opening of SFA Charter School.
The phasing out of the early childhood lab will not affect the SFA Charter School in any way, said Korbin Pate, the director of marketing and communications for the university. The Charter School enrolls kindergarten through fifth-graders and is funded primarily through the Texas Education Agency’s Foundation School Program.
Having both the charter school and the Early Childhood Laboratory together was groundbreaking, Bethel said.
“We were the first in Texas to ever have that. It was a really big deal,” she said. “It’s a great place.”
The laboratory has become an institution within the Nacogdoches community, parents, former teachers and former students say.
“It creates this connection with SFA. A lot of kids who go there, their parents don’t have a connection with SFA,” said Sydney Kroll. “It helps create a link between the community and the university.”
Kroll, whose father is an emeritus professor at SFA, attended the program as a child and sent her own son to the lab when she moved back to Nacogdoches from Austin.
“I think for a lot of professionals, not just people who work at SFA, that it’s a big draw,” Kroll said.
The Early Childhood Lab has consistently provided care and learning for children who attend over the years, but its role in developing future educators is different now, Pate said.
How Texas prepares future teachers has significantly evolved, he said, shifting toward year-long teacher residency models in public school districts. A new residency pathway mandated in 2024 by the State Board of Education was reinforced in 2025 through House Bill 2, which established a program to provide funding for teacher residency partnerships.
“As a result,” Pate said, “SFA teacher candidates now complete yearlong residencies at school districts across the state, reducing reliance on university-operated laboratory settings for many of the observation and field experiences that were more common when the Early Childhood Laboratory was established.”
Efforts to save the lab
Bethel started an online petition to save the program. As of Friday, more than 2,000 people had signed the petition on Change.org.
“It’s devastating,” Bethel said of the planned phase out of the program.
More than two dozen people have left detailed support for the lab on the petition website. Even more people have left supporting messages on her personal Facebook page where she asked SFA college of education graduates how their experiences in the lab helped shape their careers.
“There are hundreds of people who have written in. Hundreds,” she said.
She and others plan to make an appeal to SFA president Dr. Neal Weaver.
“He can be the one to make a difference. He’s got skills to do that and we could really use that,” Bethel said.
Additionally, a private Facebook group called ECHL was formed after the phasing out announcement. It currently has more than 200 members. The group is made up of parents, community members, alumni and current and former employees of the lab.
“Our immediate focus is on organizing our efforts and requesting an opportunity to meet with university leadership so we can better understand how this decision was made and engage in constructive dialogue. Out of respect for that process, we are not offering additional public comment at this time,” a member of the group said in a message to The Daily Sentinel.
summary: “Ultimately, university leadership determined that the continuing operation is no longer financially sustainable,” SFA provost Jordan Barkley said in a statement announcing the phasing out of the program. The statement was made public late Tuesday on the Facebook page of the SFA Early Childhood Laboratory by program director Crystal Sanders. “It helps create a link between the community and the university.” Kroll, whose father is an emeritus professor at SFA, attended the program as a child and sent her own son to the lab when she moved back to Nacogdoches from Austin.
